advisor_identified: Historian of medicine in McGill University’s Department of Social Studies of Medicine; supervisor of Noémi R. Tousignant’s 2006 McGill dissertation.

doctorate.institution: State University of New York at Stony Brook (Stony Brook University)
doctorate.title: The Academic Elite and the Movement to Reform French Higher Education, 1850-1885

evidence.says: McGill identifies George Weisz as Professor Emeritus in Social Studies of Medicine and states that he received a History PhD from Stony Brook University and a sociology doctorate from Paris 5 (Descartes).

His August 2017 CV, p. 1, lists a History PhD from Stony Brook University in 1976, a sociology Doctorat 3e cycle from Université de Paris-Descartes in 1979, and McGill faculty appointments beginning in 1978.

The editorial introduction to Rôle des Universités dans l’éducation sociale du pays (Revue française de sociologie, 1976), p. 181, footnote 1, identifies George Weisz as author of The academic elite and the movement to reform French higher education, 1850-1885, a 1976 PhD thesis at the State University of New York at Stony Brook.

The indexed title page identifies Noémi R. Tousignant’s Pain and the Pursuit of Objectivity as a McGill History doctoral thesis dated May 2006; the indexed acknowledgments, p. 7, name George Weisz as her supervisor.

notes: The linked record matches the advisor’s History PhD in institution, year and title; its 1850-85 is an abbreviated date range. His separate 1979 sociology doctorate at Paris-Descartes does not contradict this match.
